questions.question_text:
An investor deposits $\$600$ at the end of each year for $10\text{ years}$ into an account earning $5\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
Which geometric series represents the future value $FV$?

options.why: Treated as start-of-period payments (annuity due) rather than end-of-period payments.
Included 11 payments instead of 10 payments for a 10-year term.
Calculated compound interest on a single deposit rather than an annuity series.

questions.solution_text:
For end-of-year deposits, the first deposit compounds for $9$ years and the 10th deposit earns no interest.
$FV = 600 + 600(1.05) + 600(1.05)^{2} + \dots + 600(1.05)^{9}$

questions.question_text:
A sum of $\$2000$ is invested at the end of each year for $14\text{ years}$ at $6\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
Calculate the future value of the annuity to the nearest cent.

options.why: Multiplied by $(1+r)$ as if payments were made at the start of each year.
Summed the payments without adding any compound interest.
Counted only the final payment, which earns no interest, and omitted the other thirteen payments.

questions.solution_text:
The annual rate is $r=0.06$ and there are $14$ end-of-year payments. The first grows for $13$ years and the final payment earns no interest.
$FV=2000+2000(1.06)+2000(1.06)^2+\dots+2000(1.06)^{13}$
With first term $2000$, common ratio $R=1.06$ and $14$ terms,
$FV = \dfrac{2000(1.06^{14}-1)}{1.06-1}$
$= \$42\,030.04$ to the nearest cent.

questions.question_text:
Sarah deposits $\$250$ at the end of each month into an annuity paying $7.2\%$ p.a. compounded monthly.
What is the value of the investment after $4\text{ years}$? Give your answer to the nearest cent.

options.why: Used the annual interest rate of $7.2\%$ instead of the monthly rate of $0.6\%$.
Multiplied by $1.006$ for start-of-month payments instead of end-of-month payments.
Calculated simple principal total ($48 \times 250$) without compound interest.

questions.solution_text:
$r = \dfrac{0.072}{12} = 0.006$, $n = 48$
Payments and compounding are monthly. The first payment grows for $47$ months and the final payment earns no interest.
$FV=250+250(1.006)+250(1.006)^2+\dots+250(1.006)^{47}$
With first term $250$, common ratio $R=1.006$ and $48$ terms,
$FV = \dfrac{250(1.006^{48}-1)}{1.006-1}$
$= \$13\,858.75$ to the nearest cent.

questions.question_text:
A council deposits $\$1200$ at the end of each quarter into a park upgrade fund paying $4.8\%$ p.a. compounded quarterly.
Find the amount in the fund after $5\text{ years}$ to the nearest cent.

options.why: Treated the annuity as an annuity due by including an extra factor of $1.012$.
Ignored compound interest and simply calculated $20 \times 1200$.
Counted only the final quarterly payment, which earns no interest, and omitted the other nineteen payments.

questions.solution_text:
$r = \dfrac{0.048}{4} = 0.012$, $n = 5 \times 4 = 20$
Payments and compounding are quarterly. The first payment grows for $19$ quarters and the final payment earns no interest.
$FV=1200+1200(1.012)+1200(1.012)^2+\dots+1200(1.012)^{19}$
With first term $1200$, common ratio $R=1.012$ and $20$ terms,
$FV = \dfrac{1200(1.012^{20}-1)}{1.012-1}$
$= \$26\,943.51$ to the nearest cent.

questions.question_text:
Marcus deposits $\$1500$ at the end of each year for $8\text{ years}$ into a savings bond earning $6.5\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
How much interest did the investment earn? Give your answer to the nearest cent.

options.why: Reported the total future value rather than subtracting total contributions.
Used all contributions as one principal and an unjustified five-year simple-interest duration: $12000\times0.065\times5$.
Subtracted nine contributions instead of eight: $15115.30-9\times1500$.

questions.solution_text:
There are $8$ annual payments at a rate of $0.065$ per year. The first grows for $7$ years and the final payment earns no interest.
$FV=1500+1500(1.065)+1500(1.065)^2+\dots+1500(1.065)^7$
With first term $1500$, common ratio $R=1.065$ and $8$ terms,
$FV = \dfrac{1500(1.065^{8}-1)}{1.065-1} \approx \$15\,115.30$
$\text{Contributions} = 8 \times 1500 = \$12\,000$
$\text{Interest} = \dfrac{1500(1.065^8-1)}{0.065}-12000$
$= \$3115.30$ to the nearest cent.

questions.question_text:
An apprentice deposits $\$400$ at the end of each month for $3\text{ years}$ into a high-interest account earning $8.4\%$ p.a. compounded monthly.
Find the total interest earned over the $3\text{ years}$ to the nearest cent.

options.why: Stated the future value instead of subtracting the total deposits made.
Reported the total contributions made without calculating interest.
Calculated interest assuming deposits were made at the start of each month.

questions.solution_text:
$r = \dfrac{0.084}{12} = 0.007$, $n = 36$
Payments and compounding are monthly. The first payment grows for $35$ months and the final payment earns no interest.
$FV=400+400(1.007)+400(1.007)^2+\dots+400(1.007)^{35}$
With first term $400$, common ratio $R=1.007$ and $36$ terms,
$FV = \dfrac{400(1.007^{36}-1)}{1.007-1} \approx \$16\,312.40$
$\text{Total deposits} = 36 \times 400 = \$14\,400$
$\text{Interest} = \dfrac{400(1.007^{36}-1)}{0.007}-14400$
$= \$1912.40$ to the nearest cent.

questions.question_text:
A medical clinic deposits $\$10\,000$ at the end of each year for $12\text{ years}$ into an account earning $7.5\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
Calculate the total interest earned to the nearest cent.

options.why: Reported the future value without subtracting the total contributions.
Reported the twelve contributions rather than the interest earned.
Subtracted thirteen contributions instead of twelve: $184235.68-13\times10000$.

questions.solution_text:
$a=10000$, $r=0.075$, $n=12$
There are $12$ annual end-of-year payments. The first grows for $11$ years and the final payment earns no interest.
$FV=10000+10000(1.075)+10000(1.075)^2+\dots+10000(1.075)^{11}$
With first term $10000$, common ratio $R=1.075$ and $12$ terms,
$FV=\dfrac{10000(1.075^{12}-1)}{1.075-1}\approx\$184\,235.68$
$\text{Contributions}=12\times10000=\$120\,000$
$\text{Interest}=\dfrac{10000(1.075^{12}-1)}{0.075}-120000=\$64\,235.68$ to the nearest cent.

questions.question_text:
An investor deposits $\$3000$ at the end of each year for $12\text{ years}$ into an account earning $6\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
Calculate the future value of the investment to the nearest cent.

options.why: Added the twelve payments without allowing for compound interest.
Subtracted the contributions and reported interest earned instead of the future value.
Counted only the final payment, which earns no interest, and omitted the other eleven payments.

questions.solution_text:
$a=3000$, $r=0.06$, $n=12$
There are $12$ annual end-of-year payments. The first grows for $11$ years and the final payment earns no interest.
$FV=3000+3000(1.06)+3000(1.06)^2+\dots+3000(1.06)^{11}$
With first term $3000$, common ratio $R=1.06$ and $12$ terms,
$FV=\dfrac{3000(1.06^{12}-1)}{1.06-1}$
$=\$50\,609.82$ to the nearest cent.
